title: EndpointSurfaceState
description:
What VESPER can currently see of a computer or device surface. REM-011 / REM-012, SR-020 ("see screens").

THE PERCEIVE HALF OF COMPUTER AGENCY. semantic_scene.schema.json is what VESPER PRESENTS; this is what VESPER PERCEIVES of a machine. They are deliberately different types: conflating them is how a system ends up narrating its own output back to itself.

THREE PROPERTIES THAT ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE:

1. TYPED, NOT A BLOB. The surface is an element tree with roles, labels, values and geometry. A screenshot alone is not a surface state, because no post-condition can be asserted against it deterministically and no retry can be planned from it. `raw_capture_ref` may accompany the tree; it may never replace it.

2. UNTRUSTED BY CONSTRUCTION. `trust_class` is fixed to `retrieved_external`. Text on a screen is written by whoever wrote the screen. An instruction read off a machine is an untrusted input, and the endpoint is where it is most convincing (INV-ACT-3, INV-AUTH-6).

3. IT EXPIRES. `valid_until` is required and there is no edge from expiry to the previous value. Past `valid_until` the only readable value is UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN is not falsy: a precondition over an expired surface does not fire (INV-COORD-2, SM-WORLD-FACT).

NO MARKDOWN, NO HTML, NO free-form rich text field exists here. The same closed-vocabulary discipline INV-SCENE-3 applies to output is applied to input.

node_id.description: Cryptographic node identity (ADR-007), not a product name (INV-HW-1).

surface_ref.description: Stable handle for the surface within the node: window id, path, document url, service name.

valid_until.description: REQUIRED. After this the surface reads UNKNOWN. A screen has a shorter TTL than almost anything else in the world model.

capture_path.description: HOW this was read. INV-ACT-2 compares this against the actuating adapter: an observation captured through the acting path does not close an episode.

actuator_path.description: The adapter that acted, when this observation follows an action. DF-ENDPOINT-OBSERVE refuses a plan whose sensor_id equals this.

trust_class.description: Structurally fixed. There is no value of this field that would let screen content raise authority. A schema permitting `owner_direct` here would make the most convincing injection surface in the system also the most trusted.

confidence.description: OCR and accessibility trees are both lossy. An element read at low confidence is not a fact.

elements.description: The typed element tree. Empty is legitimate and means 'nothing readable was found', which is distinct from UNKNOWN.

role.description: Closed enum. `unknown_role` is honest and usable; an open string field would let an adapter smuggle arbitrary structure past every consumer.

text_regions.description: OCR output where no accessibility tree is available. Each region carries its own confidence; a low-confidence region is evidence, not a reading.

raw_capture_ref.description: Optional pointer to raw media, subject to INV-PRIV-3 retention (not persisted beyond the processing window). It ACCOMPANIES the element tree and never substitutes for it: a post-condition cannot be asserted deterministically against an image.

unknown_person_present.description: When true, derived inference is suppressed and the sensor moves to PAUSED (SM-SENSOR, INV-PRIV-1).

indicator_driven.description: Whether the capture indicator was verifiably ON. A capture recorded with this false is a contract violation, not a degraded reading (INV-PRIV-4).
